observation.visible_scene: A winter hilltop landscape under a low sun. The foreground is a dense field of feathery grass/seed heads coated in white frost or snow. A mid-ground ridge carries a few dark, snow-dusted bushes/trees. To the left a snow-covered valley or town spreads out; to the right a bank of low fog/cloud sits on the horizon. The sun hangs near the center, partly behind a horizontal cloud band, with a bright halo and, at the start, a distinct vertical starburst ray projecting downward from its core. The sky holds scattered clouds with a diagonal streak at upper left.
visible_changes: The downward vertical flare/spike below the sun's core, prominent in the first frames, progressively fades and is absent by the later frames.

The glow/haze immediately around the sun intensifies and spreads upward and outward, while the horizontal cloud band in front of the sun becomes brighter and more diffuse, reducing its sharp silhouette.
The overall sky tone shifts from a cooler, clearer look to a hazier, warmer wash of light around the sun; the cloud masses on the right appear to soften/drift slightly.
The frost-covered grass, the ridge bushes, the snow-covered town on the left, and the horizon line remain in fixed positions with no discernible motion.
The framing (horizon, town, foreground edges) stays constant, indicating no pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the clip is real-time or a sped-up timelapse, which determines whether the sun's apparent change is actual motion or cloud/exposure effect.
The direction of any cloud drift and what lies beyond the crop boundaries at both ends.
Whether the brightening continues or reverses after the last frame.
uncertain_details: The cause of the growing halo and fading spike (cloud thinning in front of the sun vs. camera exposure change) cannot be distinguished from the frames alone.
Subtle cloud movement on the right is hard to confirm against haze changes.
No wind-induced sway of the foreground grass is clearly supported; apparent pixel differences may be compression.
